decisions.reason: As a core airfield-lighting control extension with strong strategic fit and likely bundling into larger projects, it is probably at or near aspiration and worth retaining despite weaker recent visibility.

This surveillance display fits the integrated-operations portfolio, but its lack of recent prominence suggests results may be less clearly above aspiration, so management would keep it while monitoring closely rather than exit immediately.
A broad airport-systems training program complements the installed base, uses existing know-how and service teams, and can be carried with available slack unless performance clearly falls short.

As a narrower training course with limited strategic distinctiveness, it is the most plausible candidate to fall below aspiration and have its resources redeployed into broader training and core system offerings.

Collaborative airport software is closely aligned with the firm's direction toward real-time information sharing and integrated decision-making, so boundedly rational management would continue backing it.

Because the MLAT system is a flagship product in a growing, R&D-intensive surveillance area, management is likely to tolerate uncertainty and retain it unless there is clear evidence of serious underperformance.
